record.context_brief: Isomorphism between A_q, q-Onsager, and a coideal subalgebra
record.original_question: Let q be a non-root of unity. The q-Onsager algebra is the algebra generated by W_0 and W_1 subject to the pair of q-Dolan-Grady type relations written in the paper, namely [W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=ρ[W_0,W_1] and [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=ρ[W_1,W_0], where [X,Y]_q=qXY-q^{-1}YX and ρ is a scalar. The algebra A_q is an infinite-dimensional current algebra introduced in terms of generators {W_{-k}, W_{k+1}, G_{k+1}, G̃_{k+1} | k ∈ ℤ_+} whose first modes satisfy the same pair of relations. There is also an explicit homomorphism from the q-Onsager algebra to a coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) sending W_0 to k_+e_1 + k_-q^{-1}f_1q^{h_1} + ε_+q^{h_1}, W_1 to k_-e_0 + k_+q^{-1}f_0q^{h_0} + ε_-q^{h_0}, and ρ to (q+q^{-1})^2k_+k_-. Show that these three infinite-dimensional algebras — A_q, the q-Onsager algebra, and that coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) — are isomorphic.

evidence.quote: Studying in details the algebraic structure of the most general (non-scalar) solution of the reflection equation algebra - the so-called Sklyanin operator [Sk] - an infinite dimensional current algebra called Aq was identified in 2005 [BK], which first modes satisfy the above pair of relations. Precisely, Aq is defined in terms of generators {Wk, Wk+1, Gk+1, G˜ k+1|k ∈ Z+} and defining relations given in [BK].
According to a certain choice of coproduct structure for Uq(slc2), it reads W0 ↦ k+e1 + k−q−1 f1q h1 + ǫ+q h1 , W1 ↦ k−e0 + k+q−1 f0q h0 + ǫ−q h0 , ρ ↦ (q + q−1 )2 k+k−.
Problem 1-a: Show that the infinite dimensional algebra Aq, the q−Onsager algebra and the above coideal subalgebra of Uq(slc2) are isomorphic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a field $\mathbb{F}$ and a nonzero scalar $q\in\mathbb{F}$ that is not a root of unity. Set $[X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX$ and $[X,Y]=XY-YX$.

(1) Define the q-Onsager algebra $O_q$ as the unital associative $\mathbb{F}$-algebra with generators $W_0, W_1$ subject to the q-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_0,W_1], \qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_1,W_0],$$
where $\rho\in\mathbb{F}$ is a fixed scalar.

(2) Define the algebra $\mathcal{A}_q$ to be the unital associative $\mathbb{F}$-algebra with generators
$\{\mathcal{W}_{-k},\mathcal{W}_{k+1},\mathcal{G}_{k+1},\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{k+1} : k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\}$
subject to the standard "alternating" defining relations of the current algebra associated with the reflection equation algebra (so that, in particular, the lowest modes $W_0:=\mathcal{W}_0$ and $W_1:=\mathcal{W}_1$ satisfy the q-Dolan–Grady relations above with the same $\rho$).

(3) Inside the quantum affine algebra $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$ with Chevalley generators $e_i,f_i,q^{\pm h_i}$ ($i=0,1$), and for fixed scalars $k_\pm,\varepsilon_\pm\in\mathbb{F}$, let $\mathcal{B}\subset U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$ be the subalgebra generated by
$$\mathcal{W}_0 := k_+ e_1 + k_- q^{-1} f_1 q^{h_1} + \varepsilon_+ q^{h_1}, \qquad \mathcal{W}_1 := k_- e_0 + k_+ q^{-1} f_0 q^{h_0} + \varepsilon_- q^{h_0},$$
which is a left (or right) coideal subalgebra; assume $\rho = (q+q^{-1})^2 k_+ k_-$.

Question: Are the three infinite-dimensional algebras $\mathcal{A}_q$, $O_q$, and $\mathcal{B}$ mutually isomorphic as associative $\mathbb{F}$-algebras?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work of Terwilliger (2021, Comm. Math. Phys.) established that $\mathcal{A}_q$ is not isomorphic to $O_q$ but rather to a central extension: there is an algebra isomorphism $\mathcal{A}_q \cong O_q \otimes \mathbb{F}[z_1, z_2, \ldots]$, with $\mathcal{A}_q$ identified as the "alternating central extension" of the q-Onsager algebra. The q-Onsager algebra is known to embed as a coideal subalgebra of $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$ via the explicit homomorphism, but the threefold isomorphism originally posed is corrected: the correct relation is a central extension, not an isomorphism, of $O_q$ by $\mathcal{A}_q$. So the question is resolved, but in a refined form.

status_evidence.title: The Alternating Central Extension of the q-Onsager Algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Using a PBW basis, the current algebra A_q is isomorphic to O_q ⊗ F[z_1,z_2,...]; multiplication map ⟨W_0,W_1⟩⊗Z → O_q is an isomorphism (standard tensor product factorization).
status_evidence.claim: A_q is the alternating central extension of O_q; it is not isomorphic to O_q itself but to O_q tensored with a polynomial algebra in central generators.

status_evidence.title: The q-Onsager algebra and its alternating central extension
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses A_q as the alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra, with explicit relationship to coideal subalgebras of U_q(sl2-hat).
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the precise relationship between A_q, O_q, and coideal subalgebras of U_q(sl2-hat).
